## Overview

Today the ai-developer-toolkit lives at `D:/ai-developer-toolkit` as a sibling repo with three remotes (`origin`=evmitran_microsoft, `personal`=Evyatar108, `gim-home`=marketplace source). Codexu references it via absolute paths in `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`, `.mcp.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, several `plans/*.md` files, `.agents/memory/*.md` auto-memory, and 16 task prompts inside `.ralph-overview/data.json`. This is fragile (breaks on any other machine layout) and prevents codexu from version-pinning the toolkit commit it depends on. The codex/ submodule already follows the gim-home-URL precedent; this plan converts ai-developer-toolkit into a real git submodule of codexu under the same model, rewrites tracked absolute-path references to repo-relative form, and adds a default CI invariant that validates the documented "active plugin versions" block and the pinned submodule metadata without fetching the private toolkit submodule.

This is a HIGH-coordination structural change. **Pre-flight blocker RESOLVED 2026-06-02 by the lead** (see `preflight-approval.md`): all 3 toolkit remotes (`origin`=evmitran_microsoft, `personal`=Evyatar108, `gim-home`=marketplace source) are now synced to `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`, the submodule pin SHA is decided, and the submodule URL is `evmitran_microsoft/ai-developer-toolkit` (operator override). The plan addresses rollback, cross-machine consequences, marketplace-plugin-install coexistence, and dual-engine (Copilot CLI + Claude Code) compatibility.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

- Codexu is a pnpm@10.11.0 monorepo with workspaces under `packages/*` and a pinned `codex/` git submodule. Root `pnpm test` is a no-op via `vitest.config.ts`; CI (`typecheck.yml`, `cli-smoke-test.yml`) only watches specific packages.
- The resolver wrapper at `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (lines 67-95) has a 6-step plugin-resolution cascade: `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` env → `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/` → `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/cache/...` → `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/<latest>` → `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/` → **`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/` (local-dev fallback at line 92)**. Only the last step changes.
- `.mcp.json` (3 lines of `args`) still references `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/launch.cjs`, and tracked `.claude/settings.json` still has `"enabledMcpjsonServers": ["ralph-overview"]` while `enabledPlugins` contains only `"crews@ai-developer-toolkit": true`. AGENTS.md line 18 explicitly claims the MCP entry and `enabledMcpjsonServers` entry "have been removed" — the tracked files contradict the documentation. **Decision**: migrate `.claude/settings.json` by removing the stale `enabledMcpjsonServers` entry and adding `"ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit": true` to `enabledPlugins`, then delete `.mcp.json` (the marketplace plugin registration is the active path; the file is dev-mode leftover).
- Spawn-launchers (`.crews/spawn-launchers/*.ps1`) reference CACHED-plugin paths (`C:\Users\evmitran\.copilot\installed-plugins\ai-developer-toolkit\crews\tools\crews.js`), NOT `D:/ai-developer-toolkit`. Auto-generated by the crews plugin's `spawnMember()`. **No manual rewrite needed** — the operator brief's concern about launcher paths does not apply.
- `.ralph-overview/data.json`: 16 tracked tasks have `prompts.brainstorm|plan|impl` or kanban text referencing drive-qualified toolkit paths (`D:/ai-developer-toolkit`, `D:\\ai-developer-toolkit`, `C:/ai-developer-toolkit`, `C:\\ai-developer-toolkit`). Generated `snapshot.json` + `overview.html` regenerate from data.json via `pnpm sync-ralph-state` — never hand-edit.
- 160 `.ralph/jobs/*/plan.md`/`.txt`/`.json` files also contain the path but are historical in-flight committed state from past jobs. **Leave as-is per operator brief.** Same for `.ralph/brainstorms/<job>/selected-direction.md` (~2-3 files) and `.ralph/investigations/<topic>/*.md` (a few files).
- Plugin versions live in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, **NOT in `package.json`** (the latter often says `1.0.0`). Active versions: ralph-overview `2.7.0`, crews `3.0.0`, ralph-orchestration `5.47.0`.
- Codex submodule precedent (`.gitmodules` URL = `https://github.com/gim-home/codex.git`; local extra remotes `personal`, `work`, `codex-patched` added by operator post-clone, NOT tracked in `.gitmodules`) is the working model for the new toolkit submodule.

### Technical Constraints

- **PRE-FLIGHT BLOCKER RESOLVED (2026-06-02 by lead)**: all 3 toolkit remotes (`gim-home/main`, `evmitran_microsoft/main`, `Evyatar108/main`) are now aligned at `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`. The original-plan framing of "gim-home lags origin" was inverted — gim-home was actually 1 commit AHEAD with the crews v3.0.1 fix; the lead force-pushed it to `origin` and `personal` to align all 3. The pin SHA is `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`. No further sync is needed. The impl member MUST NOT issue `git push` to any toolkit remote. See `preflight-approval.md`.
- **Two-commit flow** for any toolkit edit post-integration (matches codex/ precedent): edit in submodule → commit there → commit gitlink pointer in codexu. Bookkeeper crew is already trained for this via codex/.
- **MAX_PATH risk** (Windows MAX_PATH = 260 chars). Codexu lives at `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/` (28 chars). Adding `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/<plugin>/node_modules/<deep nested>` could approach the limit. Mitigation: spot-check after first `pnpm install` in the submodule; the architect could not enumerate the deepest path remotely.
- **Marketplace install coexistence**: `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/` (Copilot CLI) and `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/` (Claude Code) are independent of the submodule and remain marketplace-driven. The submodule is for version-pinning + dev-mode editing, NOT for replacing the runtime install. `copilot plugin update ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit` continues to pull from gim-home, NOT from the submodule.
- **CI trigger paths**: existing workflows (`typecheck.yml`, `cli-smoke-test.yml`) only watch specific package paths. Neither runs for `.gitmodules`, `AGENTS.md`, `.ralph-overview`, or submodule-pointer changes. GitHub Actions path filters see a submodule pointer update as the gitlink path `ai-developer-toolkit`, not as files inside the submodule, so the invariant check needs either a new workflow or an extension of `typecheck.yml` with `paths:` triggers including `.gitmodules`, `AGENTS.md`, `ai-developer-toolkit`, and `tools/check-toolkit-submodule-invariants.mjs`.
- **CI invariant is metadata-only by default**: `evmitran_microsoft/ai-developer-toolkit` is private (like `gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit`), but evmitran_microsoft is the same org that already powers codexu's existing CI — no special PAT is required. The default CI invariant must NOT require `actions/checkout` `submodules: true`; it should read only checked-out codexu files plus the gitlink SHA from `git ls-tree HEAD ai-developer-toolkit`. There is no PAT-gated deep-check step in CI under this override — the optional `--deep` mode of the invariant script is retained as a local-dev affordance only (runs against an already-initialized submodule on a developer's machine), and CI does not invoke it. The previous `GIM_HOME_PAT` secret-provisioning plan is obsolete.
- The in-tree submodule is **dev-mode only**, not production: a freshly-initialized submodule doesn't have plugin `node_modules`, so `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`'s `existsPluginAt()` check (which requires `node_modules/chokidar`) fails until `pnpm install` runs inside the plugin. Cached marketplace paths must stay first in the resolver cascade — they already do.

## Approach

### Architecture

The migration is a structural git change followed by a path-rewrite sweep. The submodule add is a single atomic commit; path-rewrites are split per file-category so reviewers can verify each subsystem independently. The resolver wrapper change is the only behavior-changing modification; everything else is documentation/data updates.

Key design decisions:

1. **Submodule URL = evmitran_microsoft** (operator override 2026-06-02; the codex/ submodule precedent pins gim-home/codex.git, but the operator chose to pin the toolkit against evmitran_microsoft instead so the org matches codexu's own `origin` remote — see `preflight-approval.md`). Operator's `personal` and `gim-home` remotes are added after `git submodule update --init` and are NOT tracked in `.gitmodules`.
2. **`.mcp.json` is DELETED and `.claude/settings.json` is migrated** (not repointed). The implementation must make AGENTS.md's marketplace-registration claim true by removing `"ralph-overview"` from `enabledMcpjsonServers` (or removing the array if empty), adding `"ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit": true` to `enabledPlugins`, and deleting the stale dev-mode `.mcp.json`. This resolves the tracked config/doc contradiction and reduces drift surface.
3. **`bin/ralph-overview.mjs` local-dev fallback uses `import.meta.url`-relative resolution** (resolve `../ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview` from the script's directory, not from `process.cwd()`). This works regardless of where the user `cd`s and is portable across drive layouts.
4. **`.ralph-overview/data.json` rewrite scope = `lifecycle: tracked` tasks only**. Merged/archived tasks' historical seeds stay as history. The bulk-rewrite normalizes future plan-seed text without polluting the bookkeeping audit trail.
5. **CI invariant** is a Node script with a no-submodule-fetch default mode: verify `.gitmodules` declares `ai-developer-toolkit`, verify `git ls-tree HEAD ai-developer-toolkit` returns a pinned gitlink SHA, and verify the NEW "Active plugin versions" block in `AGENTS.md` is present and well-formed (plugin names + semver values). The block lives in a single, well-marked section so the invariant script doesn't false-positive on historical version mentions. A `--deep` mode is retained in the script as a local-dev affordance only (run by a developer against an already-initialized submodule); under the 2026-06-02 operator override CI does NOT invoke `--deep` and does NOT use a `GIM_HOME_PAT` secret. Wired into `typecheck.yml` via `paths:` triggers (or a dedicated workflow file — implementer's call).
6. **Submodule-FIRST sequencing** vs queued overview-data-* tasks. None of those tasks are actively in flight (all are `lifecycle: tracked` with no ralph stage). Concentrating path-rewrite churn in this PR is cleaner than a multi-PR rolling sweep.

### Implementation Strategy

Single feature branch (`ralph/plan-ai-developer-toolkit-submodule` → impl on `ralph/ai-developer-toolkit-submodule`). Phase ordering inside the impl:

1. **Phase 1 — pre-flight + submodule add** (US-001). Must complete first; everything else depends on the `ai-developer-toolkit/` directory existing.
2. **Phase 2 — path rewrite** (US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005 run in parallel). Disjoint file footprints.
3. **Phase 3 — CI invariant** (US-006). Depends on US-003 because the invariant script reads an AGENTS.md "Active plugin versions" block that US-003 adds.
4. **Phase 4 — smoke test + rollback docs** (US-007). Depends on all earlier phases.

Mid-flight test gates (after each phase): `pnpm sync-ralph-state` (verifies resolver still finds plugin) + `pnpm overview` (verifies watcher) + a smoke `node ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/crews.js --help` (verifies in-tree plugin shape).

### Out of Scope

- User-global memory at `C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/projects/D--harness-efforts-codexu/memory/*.md` — operator-machine-local, not tracked by codexu. Surface as a follow-up.

- Rewriting `lifecycle: merged` or `lifecycle: archived` task entries in `data.json` (their `shipManifest.commits[].oneLine` text is historical record).
- Modifying cached marketplace install paths under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` or `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/` (those are install artifacts, not source).
- Pushing changes to any ai-developer-toolkit remote (`gim-home`, `evmitran_microsoft`, `Evyatar108`). The lead pre-resolved the remote-sync at impl start; no `git push` to a toolkit remote is in scope for this impl.

## Risk Areas

- **Pre-flight blocker risk** (largely moot post-override): the lead pre-resolved the pin SHA (`d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`) and the 3-remote sync. As a defensive check, the US-001 iteration agent still runs `git -C ai-developer-toolkit rev-parse HEAD` immediately after `submodule add` — if it doesn't match `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`, deinit and re-add against the correct ref. See `preflight-approval.md`.
- **MAX_PATH overflow** during plugin `pnpm install` inside the submodule. Mitigation: spot-check `Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.FullName.Length -gt 250 }` after first install. If hit, document as a known limitation in AGENTS.md and recommend not running `pnpm install` inside the submodule on this machine; instead use the marketplace cache for runtime + submodule for source-reading only.
- **Resolver wrapper regression**: changing line 92 of `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` from absolute to `import.meta.url`-relative could break if `import.meta.url` returns an unexpected format on Windows. Test by running `pnpm sync-ralph-state` from multiple cwds (repo root, subdir, worktree path) under both Claude Code and Copilot CLI before merging.
- **`.mcp.json` deletion / Claude config migration regression**: if any other tool (not just Claude Code / Copilot CLI) reads `.mcp.json`, deletion breaks it; if `.claude/settings.json` is not migrated in the same commit, tracked Claude config points at a removed MCP server. Mitigation: `git log .mcp.json` to find who last touched it + grep the toolkit/codexu for any code that reads `.mcp.json` paths. If safe, remove `"ralph-overview"` from `enabledMcpjsonServers` (or remove the array if empty), add `"ralph-overview@ai-developer-toolkit": true` under `enabledPlugins`, delete `.mcp.json`, and update AGENTS.md line 18 to describe the now-true tracked state. If `.mcp.json` must be retained for another tool, repoint it to `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/launch.cjs` and keep the Claude config consistent with that decision.
- **CI invariant false positives**: the version-string scanner could match historical mentions in `plans/*.md` or `.agents/memory/*.md`. Mitigation: scope the scanner to ONE specific AGENTS.md section bounded by HTML comment markers (e.g., `<!-- BEGIN: active-plugin-versions -->...<!-- END: active-plugin-versions -->`), NOT a repo-wide grep.
- **CI private-submodule fetch — N/A under override**: `evmitran_microsoft/ai-developer-toolkit` is private but uses the same standard CI credentials as the rest of evmitran_microsoft's CI; the required CI invariant is metadata-only and reads from the superproject checkout (`.gitmodules`, `AGENTS.md`, and `git ls-tree HEAD ai-developer-toolkit`) without ever needing to fetch the submodule. No `GIM_HOME_PAT` or equivalent secret is required. The optional `--deep` mode of the invariant script is a local-dev affordance only and is NOT invoked from CI.
- **Submodule pointer drift**: after merge, the submodule pointer in codexu is pinned to `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7` (the operator-approved pin SHA). Future toolkit updates require a follow-up `cd ai-developer-toolkit && git pull && cd .. && git add ai-developer-toolkit && git commit` flow. Document explicitly.
- **Marketplace install drift**: an operator could update `copilot plugin update` independently of the submodule pointer, causing local expectations to differ from the documented block. Mitigation: the required CI invariant validates the checked-in AGENTS.md block and gitlink metadata only; exact manifest comparison belongs to the optional PAT-backed deep check against the pinned submodule SHA, NOT to a pre-commit hook on the operator's machine.
- **Spawn-launcher regeneration delay**: existing `.crews/spawn-launchers/*.ps1` files contain cached-plugin paths that are valid (not D:/ai-developer-toolkit), so no immediate regeneration needed. New spawns auto-use the current crews plugin source.
- **Toolkit-remote push approval — N/A under override**: the lead pre-resolved the 3-remote sync to `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7` before impl start, so the impl member never issues `git push` to any toolkit remote. See `preflight-approval.md`.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

### US-001: Pre-flight sync + submodule add
**Description:** As the bookkeeper, I want the ai-developer-toolkit added as a git submodule of codexu at a verified SHA so that codexu can version-pin its toolkit dependency.

**Key tasks:**
- **Preflight is RESOLVED (2026-06-02 by lead, recorded in `preflight-approval.md`).** Do NOT prompt the operator. Do NOT issue `git push` to any toolkit remote. The lead pre-synced all 3 toolkit remotes to `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7` and decided the pin SHA + URL override before this impl started.
- Verify clean `D:/ai-developer-toolkit` working tree (no uncommitted changes) as a defensive check — this only confirms the local checkout is sane; it does NOT gate the submodule-add.
- `cd D:/harness-efforts/codexu && git submodule add https://github.com/evmitran_microsoft/ai-developer-toolkit.git ai-developer-toolkit`
- `git submodule update --init`
- `git -C ai-developer-toolkit rev-parse HEAD` — verify equals `d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7`. If it does not match, deinit (`git submodule deinit -f ai-developer-toolkit && git rm --cached ai-developer-toolkit && rm -rf .git/modules/ai-developer-toolkit ai-developer-toolkit`) and re-add against the correct ref; never proceed with a wrong-SHA submodule.
- Single commit: `chore: add ai-developer-toolkit submodule at d7e01874385c13e7e833a6935d7de11ea2e565f7` (or short form `chore: add ai-developer-toolkit submodule at d7e01874`).

**Dependencies:** None (this is the foundation).

**Estimated complexity:** small. Preflight is resolved, so the original "medium when sync is blocked" scenario does not apply.

**Description:** As the operator landing this change, I want a recorded smoke test confirming the system still works end-to-end, plus a rollback procedure so I can recover if a regression appears post-merge.

**Dependencies:** US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006 (smoke test exercises the full integrated system; rollback docs need all the structural changes to be in place to describe what they undo).
